title: Autopilot Runbook Catalog Gateway: policy-driven admin utilities exposure
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description: Build a lightweight internal gateway that exposes curated runbook snippets and admin utilities as policy-controlled, sandboxed tasks. The gateway will allow support and SRE tooling to invoke parameterized runbook steps (e.g., rotate-key, restart-pool, collect-diagnostics) via authenticated API calls while enforcing RBAC, rate limits, dry-run and telemetry attachments. This is intended to reduce manual repetitive steps, minimize blast radius during oncall, and provide a discoverable catalog for solutions engineers.
background: We currently have many ad-hoc admin scripts and operator runbooks spread across repos and docs. Oncall frequently copy/pastes shell snippets and asks SREs to run privileged commands. Previous efforts created runnable playlets and a runbook DSL, but there's no central controlled surface that exposes vetted actions while preserving auditability and safety. The gateway will sit between the Console and internal tooling (CLI, runbook UI) and the underlying executor (operator agent / ephemeral worker pool).
goals: Provide a catalog API returning typed actions with parameter schemas and safe defaults
Enforce RBAC per action and per parameter (e.g., disable destructive flags for mid-level roles)
Support dry-run/simulate mode with structured diffs and risk scoring
Attach telemetry (trace id, action metadata) and append to audit logs and runbook timelines
Offer a graceful fallback: simulated execution results if executor unavailable
non_goals: Expose arbitrary SSH shells or unrestricted scripts
Create new long-lived privileged agents (we will reuse Operator Sidecar / Executor infra)
acceptance_criteria: Catalog endpoint returns JSON list of actions with id, title, description, parameter schema, risk_level and example payload
Execute endpoint enforces RBAC and returns a task id; task lifecycle emits events to existing runbook timeline and Audit Log
Dry-run mode returns simulated plan and delta without changing state
Telemetry appears in Console traces and the action emits custom metrics (action_invocations_total, action_failures_total, action_duration_seconds)
Rate limiting blocks excessive automated invocations and surfaces 429s with guidance
design_notes: We will leverage the typed runlet format (yaml) that the runbook DSL currently uses. The gateway will perform lightweight static validation of parameter types and call the executor via gRPC with a signed invocation token. For safety, destructive actions must require two approvals in UI mode or an escalation token in CLI mode. The catalog will include a version field so Consumers can pin action versions.
implementation_plan: API schema and contract (swagger) — small team design review
Catalog importer: transform existing curated runbooks into typed actions
RBAC enforcement module using Console's policy service
Executor integration: add grpc adapter to existing Operator Sidecar
Telemetry + Audit wiring: span propagation and audit log entries
Feature flag rollout in two stages: internal beta -> org-wide opt-in
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: exposing destructive actions — Mitigation: default to read-only/dry-run and require explicit elevated token with time-limited scope
Risk: wrong parameter validation causing failed runs — Mitigation: pre-execution schema validation and pre-run simulation checks
Risk: increased attack surface — Mitigation: require mTLS between gateway and executor, short-lived tokens, and forbid exec from public subnets
observability: Actions must emit structured events into the existing runbook timeline service. Add metrics for invocations, failures, latency. Dashboards to show top actions by invocation, average time to resolution for action-assisted incidents, and failure heatmaps by action and role.
security_considerations: All invocations are authenticated via internal OIDC. Gateway will call KMS for any secrets and never persist plaintext secrets. Elevated actions will require ephemeral tokens created via the escalation service. Every invocation must write a tamper-evident audit record (user, role, params, ip, invocation_id, timestamp).
qa_steps: Unit tests for parameter schema validation and RBAC checks
Integration tests: gateway <-> operator sidecar in staging cluster
Chaos test: simulate executor unavailability and ensure dry-run fallback returns simulated output
Pen test: scoped internal pentest focusing on token issuance and audit logs
rollout_plan: Start with 3 internal teams (SRE, Support, Platform) behind a feature flag. Collect telemetry and incident feedback for 2 weeks. Expand to all internal users if no high-severity safety incidents. Post-rollout, run a 30-day retrospective and add additional safety policy rules as needed.
